paper.title: TongUI: Internet-Scale Trajectories from Multimodal Web Tutorials for Generalized GUI Agents
paper.central_claim: Converting multimodal web tutorials (WikiHow/Baidu Experience articles and YouTube/Bilibili videos) into GUI trajectories via crawl -> text/visual processing -> zero-shot-agent (UI-TARS) thought/action generation -> multi-stage filtering yields GUI-Net-1M (1M trajectories, 5 OS, 280+ apps); fine-tuning Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B/32B on it improves grounding and navigation benchmarks, outperforming baseline agents by about 10% on multiple benchmarks and generalising across platforms.

provenance.session_note: actual_model taken from the worker system prompt (Sonnet 5.5, claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]); no session id / receipt exposed to the worker, so null

sections_read: Method (Formulation, Tutorial Source/Crawling/Process, Trajectory Generation, Data Filtering, Agent Tuning)
Experiments (Setting, Grounding, Offline/Online Navigation, User Study)
Appendix A-D (metrics, architecture, action space, resources, prompts, data scaling, error bar, AndroidControl, GUI Odyssey, examples)
materials.note: HTML text render of v4 read in full including appendix tables; figures (Fig 1-3, 5-17, prompts shown as figures) are not in the text.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we propose the TongUI framework that transforms millions of multimodal web tutorials into GUI trajectories for generalized GUI agents.
evidence.support_explanation: Central framework claim.

evidence.quote: outperforming baseline agents by 10% on multiple benchmarks
evidence.support_explanation: Headline improvement claim (holds only for specific comparisons such as UI-Vision vs ShowUI-2B).

evidence.quote: the lack of large-scale, diverse, and well-structured GUI trajectory data continues to be a key bottleneck in developing robust and generalized GUI agents.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: data scarcity/diversity; asserted, not measured on a concrete coverage dimension.

evidence.quote: Unlike them, we directly collect multimodal tutorials from the Internet and propose a multimodal tutorial process pipeline to convert them into trajectories without any simulators.
evidence.support_explanation: Delta vs AgentTrek/Synatra (tutorial -> trajectory via LLM/simulator replay).

evidence.quote: we use a pretrained GUI agent (such as UI-TARS ( Qin et al. 2025 ) ) to generate the thought
evidence.support_explanation: Labels (thoughts, actions) are produced by a strong third-party GUI model; the student is partly distilled from it.

evidence.quote: We empirically find that using h i h_{i} leads to better performance.
evidence.support_explanation: Step-level description h_i used as query instead of task q; no numbers reported for this design choice.

evidence.quote: We discard this step and make the next action the beginning of a new trajectory.
evidence.support_explanation: Failed-format steps split trajectories (explains many 1-3 step trajectories).

evidence.quote: the agent typically predicts the action wait or call_user
evidence.support_explanation: Trajectory filter uses the teacher's wait/call_user as a GUI-irrelevance signal; then a Qwen2.5-VL-7B quality filter.

evidence.quote: Then, we feed the screenshot and trajectory of a task into a Qwen2.5-VL-7B model, and prompt it to filter out low-quality data.
evidence.support_explanation: Learned filter, not validated against human labels in the text.

evidence.quote: we directly remove exact duplicate tutorials based on their unique identifiers
evidence.support_explanation: Only exact-ID deduplication; no near-duplicate or benchmark-overlap check.

evidence.quote: After applying duplicate tutorial removal, content filtering, and trajectory filtering, 33.0% of the original data is retained.
evidence.support_explanation: Retention 33%; effect of the filter on downstream accuracy not ablated.

evidence.quote: we adopt the MOG2 algorithm
evidence.support_explanation: Key-frame extraction by background-subtraction change detection; no accuracy check of frame-step alignment.

evidence.quote: To address this issue, we prompt GPT-4o-mini to classify each image as a screenshot or not.
evidence.support_explanation: Image-type filter by an LLM.

evidence.quote: five participants with substantial experience in GUI agent research (but not involved in our project) are asked to rate the quality of each data point on a scale from 0 (very poor) to 5 (excellent)
evidence.support_explanation: Data-quality evaluation is a 0-5 rating by 5 raters on 100+100 samples, not action-accuracy against ground truth.

evidence.quote: the average score increases from 3.22 to 4.12 after filtering
evidence.support_explanation: Filtering raises rated quality; ShowUI sample scores 4.26 (higher than the filtered 4.12).

evidence.quote: the ShowUI dataset receives an average score of 4.26
evidence.support_explanation: Comparator dataset rated higher than GUI-Net after filtering; authors call this 'comparable'.

evidence.quote: we utilize the SFT data (training set) of the evaluation dataset to fine-tune the model.
evidence.support_explanation: Second-stage fine-tuning on each benchmark's training split for the navigation benchmarks.

evidence.quote: takes roughly four days for a 3B model and seven days for a 7B model
evidence.support_explanation: Training compute disclosed (8xA100-80G); data-construction cost is not.
ScreenSpot 86.0, V2 88.7, Pro 24.7 for TongUI-7B (icon accuracy on Pro 8.0).
The teacher-family model is stronger on all three grounding benchmarks (Pro 35.7 vs 24.7).

evidence.quote: TongUI | TongUI-7B | 76.0 | 91.9
evidence.support_explanation: AndroidControl High/Low step accuracy; UI-TARS-7B 72.5/90.8; whether UI-TARS was trained on the AndroidControl train split is not stated.

evidence.quote: On the AndroidControl and UI-Vision datasets, TongUI achieves even better performance than UI-TARS.
evidence.support_explanation: Author claim of beating the teacher on two offline benchmarks.

evidence.quote: Qwen2.5-VL-3B-ShowUI | ✓ \checkmark | 67.7
evidence.support_explanation: Closest same-base comparison on online MiniWob: ShowUI-data model 67.7 vs TongUI-3B 72.7 (base Qwen2.5-VL-3B 0.3, unfine-tuned).

evidence.quote: TongUI-3B | ✓ \checkmark | 72.7
evidence.support_explanation: MiniWob online score, fine-tuned per SeeClick protocol.

evidence.quote: Considering that the multimodal tutorials are offline data, the improvements confirm the generalization of TongUI.
evidence.support_explanation: Author inference from MiniWob in-domain fine-tuned results.
Control: SFT on 'refined public data' (definition not given): ScreenSpot 68.0, Mind2Web Step SR 39.7/35.5/40.7.
Adding GUI-Net data lifts ScreenSpot to 83.6 and Mind2Web Step SR to 48.8/48.1/49.5; per-source 50K additions also help (WikiHow, Baidu, Video).

evidence.quote: we conduct three independent runs on Mind2Web for each type of tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Only TongUI-3B on Mind2Web has 3 runs (SD <0.5 pp).
Baidu Experience (same source as training tutorials) task success 56.9 vs ShowUI-2B 14.7: in-source evaluation.

evidence.quote: The step is correct if and only if both of the action prediction and parameter prediction are correct.
evidence.support_explanation: Exact-match step correctness (penalises valid alternative actions).

evidence.quote: In this method, we have to collect all tutorials and train the model once, which may overlook the potential for continual learning.
evidence.support_explanation: Only stated limitation.

evidence.quote: The higher proportion of trajectories of 1-3 steps is partly due to the trajectory splitting strategy described in Section 3.5.
evidence.support_explanation: Short trajectories dominate; long-horizon coverage weak.

signatures.object: Training data: raw tutorials (video/article) -> (query, {screenshot, thought, action}) trajectories (baseline: manual or LLM-synthesised GUI datasets such as ShowUI/AGUVIS/AgentTrek)
signatures.information: Tutorial text (ASR via Whisper or article text), key frames (MOG2 on audio-segmented clips or article images), step description h_i; the UI-TARS teacher sees (o_i, h_i). No environment feedback, no ground-truth actions, no test-set information intended.
signatures.operation: Keyword crawl (LLM-expanded 'app/web+task') -> LLM extraction of task q and step descriptions -> key-frame/screenshot selection -> zero-shot UI-TARS generates thought and action per step -> failed formats split trajectories -> dedupe + LLM content filter + wait/call_user rule + Qwen2.5-VL-7B quality filter.
signatures.conditions: Works where tutorials are visual and teacher can parse the frames; desktop/mobile only ('others' discarded).
signatures.feedback: none from execution; labels come from a teacher model
signatures.selection_data: Tutorial content, teacher action tokens, Qwen2.5-VL-7B judgment.
signatures.failure_boundary: Label noise from the teacher unmeasured; 1-3 step trajectories dominate; exact-ID dedupe only.

signatures.information: Screenshot history (up to 2 previous observations), thoughts/actions history, query.
signatures.operation: LoRA (rank 16, alpha 32) SFT on GUI-Net-1M, then fine-tune on the evaluation dataset's training split for the navigation benchmarks; grounding evaluated zero-shot.
signatures.conditions: Per-benchmark second stage for navigation; MiniWob follows SeeClick fine-tuned protocol.
signatures.claimed_effect: + over base Qwen2.5-VL and over ShowUI-style baselines on ScreenSpot, AITW, Mind2Web, AndroidControl, UI-Vision, MiniWob.
signatures.failure_boundary: Below UI-TARS-7B on ScreenSpot-Pro (24.7 vs 35.7); icon grounding weak.

gap.author_gap: Generalised GUI agents lack large, diverse, cross-OS/app trajectory data: manual annotation is costly and LLM-synthesised trajectories lack diversity/accuracy.
gap.checked_gap: Data scarcity for cross-platform trajectories is a real, widely stated limitation, and AgentTrek/Synatra are the right nearest neighbours (tutorial-derived trajectories). The paper compares dataset sizes (Table 1) but does not show that existing datasets fail on a concrete coverage axis, and does not analyse the new failure mode it introduces: dependence on a stronger teacher (UI-TARS) for labels.
lineage: Manual/synthetic GUI trajectory data (AITW, AndroidControl, GUI Odyssey, ShowUI, AGUVIS) -> web-tutorial-derived data (Synatra, AgentTrek, textual tutorials + LLM/simulator) -> TongUI (multimodal tutorials, teacher-labelled, no simulator)

rs_pattern.reason: Operation actually executed: with no ground-truth trajectories at scale, a supervisory signal (thought+action labels) is manufactured by a model (UI-TARS) on crawled material and routed through a multi-stage quality gate before training. Sibling check: C07 (adaptation-process stability) and C26 (preference/reward objectives) do not apply; C08 (generate candidate instances, gate, fold back into the corpus) is the closest.
rs_pattern.executes_pattern: partial: generate-then-filter data factory is implemented; the generator is an existing teacher (not a steerable one), there is no iteration or learner-feedback loop, and the filter is not ablated downstream.
rs_pattern.resolves_problem: partially evidenced: adding GUI-Net data improves ScreenSpot and Mind2Web over an SFT-on-public-data arm (Table 12), but the diversity/coverage gap itself and teacher dependence are not measured.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: C08 steps: (1) binding constraint = corpus, cheaper non-generative remedy ruled out - partial (compared with SFT on public 'refined' data); (2) controllable generator reaching under-covered region - weak (tutorial crawl widens apps/OS but no coverage analysis; labeller is a fixed teacher); (3) one load-bearing filter argued as the crux - weak (three heterogeneous filters, none ablated downstream, only a 200-sample rating study); (4) iterate with learner feedback - absent; (5) transfer to real targets and cheaper baselines - partial (benchmarks and ShowUI-data baseline, no equal-size alternative dataset).

met: downstream benchmark evidence rather than proxy-only
failure_modes_present: generate-and-filter built on an existing teacher (thin wrapper risk)
no comparison to equal-size alternative data source

matches.reason: Matches the generate -> gate -> train structure of C08 but with a fixed teacher and unablated gates; differs from siblings C07 and C26 as stated.

condition_checks.reason: Extraction/labelling is not scored against human labels (only a 0-5 quality rating on 100+100 samples); no action-accuracy figure.
Zero-shot ScreenSpot-Pro and UI-Vision are evaluated without benchmark training, but app/site overlap between tutorials and benchmarks is not analysed.
Compared with other open data (ShowUI data model) but no per-trajectory annotation/crawl cost versus alternatives is reported.
Labelling context (step description vs task, narration, neighbouring frames) is not ablated; only 'empirically better' is asserted.
Evaluation tasks differ from tutorials (benchmarks), but the Baidu Experience evaluation comes from the same source family.
Most benchmarks are not aligned with specific tutorials; Baidu Experience is in-source.
Teacher (UI-TARS) labels are used for SFT with a learned filter but without accuracy measurement or downstream error analysis.
Mostly offline exact-match benchmarks; one online benchmark (MiniWob) is in-domain fine-tuned.
Key-frame loss and frame-step alignment are not evaluated; trajectories are mostly 1-3 steps.
Only 33% retained and 'others' category discarded; effect on coverage not quantified.
Generated thoughts are not kept only when the action matches ground truth (no ground truth exists for tutorial steps).
Single reasoning level; no mixture or decoding-level ablation.
Reasoning noise from source traces not analysed.
Three sizes of one backbone family (3B/7B/32B) but gains vs size not analysed.

unassigned: Single action schema shared across desktop and mobile (Table 8 action space) resembles planner_grounder_interface/C12, but no multi-source schema normalisation or ablation is reported, so not matched.
revision_proposals: none: R03 already covers tutorial/video-derived trajectories; TongUI adds a teacher-labelled, large-scale (1M) instance. Note for the card: teacher-dependence confound should be a listed failure mode (teacher model also used as comparison baseline).

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS C08: generate candidate training instances and pass them through a quality gate before training. Domain R03: mine human screen recordings, infer actions between key frames with a VLM and SFT. TongUI's labelling step (teacher VLM infers thought/action per tutorial frame) is the shared operation; filters play the gate.
pattern_mapping.conditions_differences: R03 expects validation of extraction/labels against humans and an ablated labelling context; TongUI has neither. C08 expects iteration or learner feedback; TongUI has none. TongUI adds article tutorials (not only video).

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Both: a strong MLLM writes the thought/action targets for demonstration steps that a screenshot policy is then SFT'd on.
pattern_mapping.conditions_differences: C21's success conditions (action-consistent reasoning, mixed levels) are not available here because tutorial steps have no ground-truth actions.

claims.text: GUI-Net-1M (1M trajectories, 5 OS, 280+ apps) can be built automatically from web tutorials at low cost with acceptable quality.
claims.baseline_control: ShowUI sample rated 4.26 vs filtered GUI-Net 4.12 by 5 raters
claims.counterevidence: Label accuracy vs ground truth not measured; construction cost not reported; unfiltered 3.22 rating.
claims.allowed_conclusion: A large tutorial-derived dataset exists with mid-high rated quality; label accuracy and 'low-cost' are unverified.

claims.text: Fine-tuning on GUI-Net-1M improves grounding over the base model and rivals/surpasses open baselines.
claims.baseline_control: base Qwen2.5-VL, ShowUI-2B, OS-Atlas, AGUVIS, UGround, UI-TARS
claims.counterevidence: Below the UI-TARS teacher family; base-model numbers are authors' reproduction (†).
claims.allowed_conclusion: Large gains over the base model; still below UI-TARS-7B.

claims.text: TongUI outperforms baselines on offline navigation (AITW, AndroidControl, Mind2Web, UI-Vision), 'even better than UI-TARS' on two.
claims.setting: benchmark training split used for second-stage fine-tuning
claims.selection_vs_test: benchmark train/test splits; teacher data unknown
claims.counterevidence: Base Qwen2.5-VL baseline is zero-shot, so its low numbers conflate format learning; whether UI-TARS got the same in-domain fine-tuning is unstated; exact-match metric.
claims.allowed_conclusion: With in-domain fine-tuning, adding GUI-Net data improves offline step metrics over an SFT-on-public-data arm (Table 12).

claims.counterevidence: Simple environment, in-domain fine-tuning, no variance.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Small in-domain online gain (+1.2 to +5.0 pp over ShowUI-based baselines) in single runs.

claims.text: Data from more sources and larger scale keeps improving performance.
claims.counterevidence: 'refined data' and 'all data' sizes unspecified; no equal-size alternative data arm; one model size.
claims.allowed_conclusion: GUI-Net data adds ~8-16 points over an unspecified public-data SFT arm on these benchmarks.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Only MiniWob provides execution-based online success and it is in-domain fine-tuned; all other evidence is offline. Strictly the claim rests mostly on offline results; 'online' is the ceiling the evidence reaches, not 'transfer'.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Authors report that adding a teacher-labelled, tutorial-derived trajectory corpus to SFT improves zero-shot grounding and offline step accuracy over the base Qwen2.5-VL and over an SFT-on-public-data arm, with TongUI-7B still below UI-TARS-7B on ScreenSpot-family; evidence for generalisation, low cost and label quality is thin.
not_supported: 'outperforming baseline agents by 10%' as a general statement
unresolved: Accuracy of UI-TARS-generated labels vs human
Overlap between tutorials and benchmark apps/sites
Definition and size of 'refined public data' and 'all data'
Whether baselines received the same per-benchmark fine-tuning
assessment.retention_trace: not_applicable: static data+SFT study; no retained/self-improving loop claimed

G.reason: Real, commonly stated limitation (cross-platform trajectory scarcity) with right neighbours (AgentTrek, Synatra) but the gap is argued by dataset-size comparison, not measured coverage/quality deficits, and the new teacher-dependence limitation is not discussed.

M.reason: Conversion pipeline is concrete (tutorial structure supplies step descriptions; teacher labels; filters) but its validity hinges on an unvalidated teacher and an unablated filter; no analysis of why tutorial-derived data should add information beyond the teacher's own knowledge.

X.reason: Sources, crawling, Whisper/MOG2 processing, teacher call, filtering stages, LoRA hyperparameters and compute are specified and the data/code are released; filter prompts/thresholds, frame-step alignment checks and per-source statistics are not in the text.

E.measurement.reason: ScreenSpot-family click-in-box and MiniWob rewards are reliable but offline exact-match step metrics penalise valid alternatives; data quality is judged by a 5-rater 0-5 study and a learned filter with no accuracy vs ground truth.

E.causality.reason: Table 12 (SFT on public data vs + GUI-Net by source) and a same-base ShowUI-data comparison give some attribution, but gains are confounded with teacher distillation (UI-TARS) and per-benchmark fine-tuning, with no equal-size alternative-data arm or filter ablation.

E.holdout.reason: Zero-shot grounding on ScreenSpot-Pro/UI-Vision is a reasonable held-out signal; but navigation benchmarks use their own train splits, Baidu Experience is in-source, no contamination/overlap analysis (exact-ID dedupe only), and the teacher's training data is opaque.

E.statistics.reason: Single runs for almost everything; 3-run error bar only for TongUI-3B on Mind2Web; no CIs, no failure analysis by error type.

E.cost.reason: Training compute disclosed, but 'low-cost' data construction (crawling, ASR, LLM and teacher calls) is not costed and baselines' compute is not matched.

rationale: TongUI 把网页图文/视频教程经 UI-TARS 逐步标注再三级过滤，得到 GUI-Net-1M 并 SFT Qwen2.5-VL。Table 12 显示加入该数据后 ScreenSpot 68.0→83.6、Mind2Web Step SR 39.7→48.8，相对基座和 ShowUI 数据基线有明确提升。主要弱点：标签来自更强的教师 UI-TARS，学生又与 UI-TARS 比较（循环/蒸馏混杂）；过滤器未做下游消融，质量只有 5 人评分；导航基准使用各自训练集二阶段微调，缺少同量级替代数据对照与污染分析；在线证据仅 MiniWob 单次。RS 原卡 primary=self_supervised_signal_engineering/C08（partial）；领域卡 mine_human_screen_videos/R03（strong）、trajectory_level_policy_training/C21（partial）。claim_support=scoped，evidence_level=online（上限）。
